text:
Tom: :rotating_light: Incident alert — EU edge DNS resolvers are returning intermittent SERVFAILs, clients in eu-west-1 seeing ~5xxs. Pager triggered at 1791012345. Investigating now.

SRE-Oncall: Acknowledged. I'm on pager. Any customer-facing errors or only internal health checks?

Tom: Customer-facing. External 503/502 spikes reported by a handful of load tests and first-party synthetic checks. Route53+Cloudflare answers diverging on some records. See quick dig from a failing probe:

Tom: ```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.prod.redwood.ai A
SERVFAIL
```

Anya: I'm on the EU shift, jumping in. Noted that Cloudflare resolver responses look slower from our probes. Can someone check Cloudflare status and Route53 change history?

Ingrid: Cloudflare status shows no global outage but there are edge errors in eu-central logs. Route53 console shows no recent changes. I started a synthetic from eu-central and got NXDOMAIN then SERVFAIL for the same name.

SRE-Oncall: Good. This smells like a resolver cache divergence between our GeoDNS layer and CF/Route53. If the GeoDNS edge has sticky cache or stale negative cache, we may be routing customers to unhealthy origins.

Tom: Deploy-bot, did we push any DNS-related config in the last 3 hours?

deploy-bot: No DNS config changes in last 6 hours. Last change was a console tweak 12h ago.

Anya: Mitigation plan suggestion: 1) Shorten GeoDNS TTL for affected zones to 30s, 2) Force failover to Route53 primary policy (bypass CF when probe fails), 3) Clear edge negative cache where supported. I'll start TTL update.

SRE-Oncall: Agree. Also open a support case with Cloudflare (ticket attached) and escalate Route53 if Route53 starts returning SERVFAIL. Ingrid, can you run a cross-region check and quantify impact? Use these commands and paste outputs.

Ingrid: Running checks now:

Ingrid: ```
$ for r in eu-west-1 eu-central-1 eu-north-1; do echo $r; dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.prod.redwood.ai A +time=2; done
eu-west-1
SERVFAIL
eu-central-1
93.184.216.34
eu-north-1
SERVFAIL
```

Ingrid: Early estimate: ~12% of EU edge probes failing, correlates with synthetic alerts and ~8% traffic error spike. Impacting a subset of customers behind certain ISPs.

Tom: Noted customer impact: some livestreams and webhooks failing. Opening internal incident ticket INC-12531 and customer-facing status note draft in #status-updates.

SRE-Oncall: Anya — do the TTL flip and set GeoDNS policy to prefer Route53 (force path). Use this DNS CLI:

SRE-Oncall: ```
# set ttl to 30s for zone
redwood-dnsctl zones update api.prod.redwood.ai --ttl 30
# switch geo policy to primary route53
redwood-dnsctl routing set api.prod.redwood.ai --policy route53-primary --force
```

Anya: Executing now.

ops-bot: Action log: TTL update initiated by Anya at 1791012442. Geo policy switch queued.

Tom: After TTL update we might still have cached SERVFAIL entries at resolvers. Plan: 1) Keep TTL low for next 30m, 2) route healthcheck traffic via Route53, 3) run negative-cache purge where provider supports it.

Ingrid: Post-change probes:

Ingrid: ```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.prod.redwood.ai A
93.184.216.34
```

Ingrid: Looks better from eu-central. Continued intermittent failures from a couple of ASNs.

SRE-Oncall: Good. Track error rate and user impact. If errors don't drop below 1% in 15m, escalate to cloud network team and open account-level Cloudflare escalation.

Anya: Oncall handoff — I'm taking the next 2 hours and will remain primary while we stabilize. @SRE-Oncall, please update me if you need to escalate.

Tom: Drafted customer status: "We're seeing partial DNS resolution issues affecting some EU customers; mitigations in progress. No config changes expected to cause this. We're routing traffic to an alternate resolver and expect improvement within 30 minutes." Posting to #status-updates now.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INC-12531 updated: mitigation in progress, owner Anya, severity: SEV3, customer impact: partial EU region failures.

SRE-Oncall: After 20m monitoring: error spike reduced from ~8% to ~1.7%. Some residual failures limited to two ISPs. Recommend extended monitoring and keep TTL 30s for one hour, then revert.

Anya: Will keep TTL at 30s and keep the route53-primary policy for 45 minutes. If stable, I'll roll TTL back to 300s and remove forced route.

Tom: Thanks team. Cloudflare support case opened with ticket #CF-987234, shared logs and asked for negative cache purge. Route53 contacted for advisory.

Ingrid: Logging note: saved dig outputs and synthetic traces to INC-12531. Will follow up on any customer DM threads.

SRE-Oncall: Closing action items: 1) Monitor for 60m, 2) revert TTL and routing if safe, 3) update incident timeline and postmortem if recurrence.

Anya: Acknowledge. Taking over monitoring.

Tom: :thumbsup: Leaving thread for now, ping me if it regresses.

SRE-Oncall: :white_check_mark: Temporary mitigation successful, moving to monitoring phase.
